input: From 1946 until 1953, Jowett Cars Ltd, a company based in Idle near Bradford, England, manufactured the Jowett Bradford, a British light van. Between 1947 and 1953, an estate car variant was also offered. Built on the foundations of the pre-war Jowett Eight, this model marked the first Jowett vehicle to return to production following World War II. Despite its simplicity, the Bradford attracted post-war consumers through its fuel efficiency and ready availability.
target: The Jowett Bradford was a British light van produced from 1946 to 1953 by Jowett Cars Ltd of Idle, near Bradford, England. It was also available as an estate car from 1947 to 1953. The vehicle was based on the pre-war Jowett Eight and was the first Jowett to be re-introduced after the Second World War. Although it was very basic, the Bradford's economy and availability appealed to the post-war market.

input: Located in Paxton, Massachusetts, Anna Maria College sponsored intercollegiate athletic programs whose teams were called the Anna Maria Amcats. Competing across 13 sports, these teams operated under NCAA Division III. The Amcats had previously been members of the Great Northeast Athletic Conference (GNAC) before transitioning to full membership in the Massachusetts State Collegiate Athletic Conference (MASCAC) starting with the 2025-26 academic year. All 13 sports programs fell under MASCAC, with the name "Amcats" serving as an acronym for Anna Maria College Athletic Team Sports. Financial hardship led to the college's permanent closure on May 10, 2026, which brought an immediate end to all of its athletic activities.
target: The Anna Maria Amcats was the nickname of the intercollegiate athletic teams of Anna Maria College, located in Paxton, Massachusetts. The school's teams participated in 13 intercollegiate sports at the NCAA Division III level. The Amcats were formerly a member of the Great Northeast Athletic Conference (GNAC), and gained full membership of the Massachusetts State Collegiate Athletic Conference (MASCAC), effective as of the 2025-26 academic year. All thirteen of Anna Maria's teams were members of the Massachusetts State Collegiate Athletic Conference (MASCAC). input: Kristoffer Wikner Sundborg, born January 20, 1993, is a retired Swedish ice hockey winger. He made his Elitserien debut during the 2011–12 season with Frölunda HC, going on to appear in 21 total games throughout the 2011–12 and 2012–13 seasons. The majority of his professional career was spent competing in the HockeyAllsvenskan and Hockeyettan leagues. In 2018, following prolonged difficulties with concussion-related recovery, Wikner made the decision to retire from ice hockey.
target: Kristoffer Wikner Sundborg (born January 20, 1993) is a Swedish retired ice hockey winger. input: *Killing 'em Softly* is a 1982 Canadian thriller directed by Max Fischer and starring Irene Cara, George Segal, Clark Johnson, and Nicholas Campbell. Today, the film is best remembered for the significant production difficulties it faced. These problems resulted in it becoming one of the first Canadian films to bypass a theatrical release and go directly to video, and they also sparked a financing dispute that remained unresolved until 1995. Adapted from Laird Koenig's novel *The Neighbor*, the plot follows a woman whose boyfriend has been murdered and who subsequently falls in love with his killer. Irene Cara also sings the film's opening theme song, "City Nights".
target: Killing 'em Softly is a 1982 Canadian thriller film directed by Max Fischer, starring Irene Cara, George Segal, Clark Johnson and Nicholas Campbell. It is most noted for production problems which led to it becoming one of the first Canadian films ever to be released direct to video, and led to a court case over production funding which was not resolved until 1995. Based on Laird Koenig's novel The Neighbor, the film's plot centres on the girlfriend of a murdered man, who falls in love with her boyfriend's killer. Irene Cara also performs the opening theme song "City Nights".

input: Maximo Yabes was born on January 29, 1932, in Lodi, California, and died on February 26, 1967. A United States Army soldier, he was posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor, America's highest military decoration, for his heroic conduct during the Vietnam War near Phu Hoa Dong in South Vietnam. Yabes demonstrated exceptional valor by shielding fellow soldiers in a bunker with his own body, relocating two injured men to a secure location for medical care, and neutralizing an enemy machine gun emplacement. He sustained fatal wounds during these actions.
target: Maximo Yabes (January 29, 1932 – February 26, 1967) born in Lodi, California, was a United States Army soldier who posthumously received the Medal of Honor — the United States' highest military decoration — for his actions near Phu Hoa Dong in South Vietnam during the Vietnam War. Yabes distinguished himself when he used his body as a shield to protect others in a bunker, moved two wounded men to a safer position where they could be given medical treatment and destroyed an enemy machine gun position before being mortally wounded.

input: The Constantin Diaconovici Loga National College (Colegiul Național Constantin Diaconovici Loga in Romanian) is a secondary school situated at 16 C. D. Loga Street in Caransebeș, Romania. The institution traces its roots back to 1582, a year in which historical records show that a teacher training school was already in operation in Caransebeș. In 1871, Ioan Popasu, the Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Caransebeș, chose to rename the school the Diocesan Pedagogical Institute. At first, the school ran a three-year program, which had been lengthened to four years by 1895. In 1919, four junior grades were introduced, a change that occurred at the same time as Transylvania's incorporation into Romania. After the communist government took power in 1948, the school lost its pedagogical focus, which was later reinstated in 1969. The main building, finished in 1899, is designated a historic monument protected by Romania's Ministry of Culture and Religious Affairs. Construction of the building's upper section started in 1924 and was completed in 1956.
target: Constantin Diaconovici Loga National College (Romanian: Colegiul Național Constantin Diaconovici Loga) is a high school located at 16 C. D. Loga Street, Caransebeș, Romania. input: Kalle Petter Huttunen, commonly referred to as Pekka (born 2 August 1871 in Rantasalmi, died 24 November 1932 in Petrozavodsk), was a Finnish tenant farmer and politician. He represented the Social Democratic Party of Finland (SDP) in the Finnish Parliament from 1907 to 1918. During the Finnish Civil War, Huttunen sided with the Red faction. After the Finnish Socialist Workers' Republic was defeated and dissolved, he moved to the Soviet Union, where he ultimately settled in the Karelian ASSR.
target: Kalle Petter (Pekka) Huttunen (2 August 1871, Rantasalmi — 24 November 1932, Petrozavodsk) was a Finnish tenant farmer and politician. He was a member of the Parliament of Finland from 1907 to 1918, representing the Social Democratic Party of Finland (SDP). During the Finnish Civil War Huttunen sided with the Reds, and after the collapse of the Finnish Socialist Workers' Republic he fled to Soviet Russia. He later settled in the Karelian ASSR.

input: Bassline—also known by various other names such as bassline house, 4x4, and niche—is a genre of electronic dance music that emerged in South Yorkshire during the early 2000s. The style is characterized by a signature four-on-the-floor rhythm playing at approximately 135–142 beats per minute, prominent bass tones reminiscent of speed garage, sliced vocal samples pulled from R&B and pop tracks, and a generally pop-oriented sensibility. In the genre's formative period, Sheffield's Niche Nightclub stood as the most important venue in the bassline scene—a position it maintained until it became the subject of public controversy when a police operation led to its permanent closure in 2005.
target: Bassline (sometimes referred to as bassline house or 4x4 or niche) is a genre of electronic dance music that originated in South Yorkshire in the early 2000s. Stylistically it comprises a four-to-the-floor beat with a tempo of around 135–142 beats per minute and a heavy bass, similar to speed garage, with chopped up R&B and Pop vocal samples and a pop music aesthetic. Particularly in the scene's early days, the most prominent bassline club was Sheffield's Niche Nightclub, which became the centre of controversy due to a police raid which resulted in the club's closure in 2005.

input: Miracle Mile is a 1988 American apocalyptic thriller written and directed by Steve De Jarnatt, starring Anthony Edwards and Mare Winningham. The film centers on the panic and turmoil that erupts following the sudden outbreak of military conflict and the looming threat of nuclear annihilation. Events play out over a single day, depicted largely in real-time. The title references the Miracle Mile neighborhood of Los Angeles, where most of the film's action takes place.
target: Miracle Mile is a 1988 American apocalyptic thriller film written and directed by Steve De Jarnatt. The film stars Anthony Edwards and Mare Winningham. Its plot depicts the panic surrounding a supposed doomsday brought on by a sudden outbreak of war and its oncoming nuclear holocaust, taking place in a single day and mostly in real-time. The title is named after the Miracle Mile neighborhood of Los Angeles where most of the events take place.

input: Pinoquio is a monotypic genus comprising South American cellar spiders, represented by the sole species Pinoquio barauna. The genus was originally named Pinocchio when first described by B. A. Huber & L. S. Carvalho in 2019, inspired by Pinocchio—the character whose prominent nose resembled the projecting clypeus observed in P. barauna. The original name proved problematic, however, as it duplicated an existing name: the harvestman genus Pinocchio Mello-Leitão, 1940 (now synonymized with Bresslauius Mello-Leitão, 1935). In response, the genus was renamed to Pinoquio in 2022, adopting the Portuguese version of Collodi's well-known character's name. The genus has been documented exclusively in Brazil.

Tunstall Healthcare, established in 1957 and headquartered in Doncaster, is a technology company specializing in digital health and care services. The company has a presence in 19 countries, employs around 3,000 people, and supports 5 million connected users worldwide, making it a significant player in the telehealth market. Emil Peters holds the position of Chief Executive Officer.

Among the company's key acquisitions are American Medical Alert Corporation (December 2011), Secuvita, a Dutch technology solutions provider serving 70,000 users (2021), and BeWo Unternehmensgruppe, a German company (2022). In January 2019, Tunstall sold Tunstall Americas to Connect America.com, a move consistent with its strategic transition toward a technology-led managed services model.

Tunstall works alongside Telefónica to provide remote patient management systems and services, strengthening its preventive care capabilities for patients living with chronic conditions. In 2019, the company jointly produced a report with hft, a charitable organization, which was launched in the House of Lords. The report explored the untapped potential of assistive technology within social care and was endorsed by the Voluntary Organisations Disability Group.
target: Tunstall Healthcare is a technology company established in 1957 which specialises in digital health and care services. Its head office is in Doncaster. input: Born on December 9, 1995, McKayla Rose Maroney is a retired American artistic gymnast. She competed as part of the Fierce Five, the American women's gymnastics team that claimed gold in the team event at the 2012 Summer Olympics, where she additionally earned a silver medal in the individual vault competition. At the 2011 World Championships, Maroney helped the American team secure gold and captured the vault championship for herself. She made history by becoming the first American female gymnast to successfully retain a World Championship vault title when she defended it at the 2013 World Championships. Earlier in her gymnastics career, she earned three gold medals competing at the 2010 Pan American Championships. A viral Internet meme emerged from a photo of Maroney displaying a "not impressed" look following her silver medal victory in vault at the 2012 Summer Olympics. After ceasing competition following the 2013 World Championships, Maroney officially retired from gymnastics in 2016.
target: McKayla Rose Maroney (born December 9, 1995) is an American former artistic gymnast. She was a member of the American women's gymnastics team, dubbed the Fierce Five, that won a gold medal in the team competition at the 2012 Summer Olympics. There, she also won an individual silver medal on the vault. Maroney was also a member of the gold-winning American team at the 2011 World Championships, where she also won the vault title. She then became the first U.S. female gymnast to defend a World Championship vault title at the 2013 World Championships. Earlier in her career, she won three gold medals at the 2010 Pan American Championships. In 2016, she retired from gymnastics after not competing since the 2013 World Championships.

input: The Kategoria e Dytë is the third tier of professional football in Albania. Known as the Second Division since the 2004–05 season, it consists of 23 teams split into two sections based on geography. The winner of each section gains promotion to the Kategoria e Parë, with both section champions then facing each other in a final to determine the overall season winner. Meanwhile, the bottom-placed teams from each section are relegated to the Kategoria e Tretë.

input: In 1564, King Sebastian of Portugal named D. Antão de Noronha as viceroy of India. Before taking on this position, he had served in Ceuta during the 1540s and held a captaincy at Hormuz throughout the 1550s. Born as an illegitimate son of João de Noronha, he was also the nephew of Afonso de Noronha, who had himself served as viceroy from 1550 to 1554. Antão de Noronha governed Portuguese India from 3 September 1564 until September 1568. One of his significant accomplishments during this time was capturing Mangalore and building a fort there in 1568. He passed away in 1569 during his sea voyage returning to Portugal.
target: D. Antão de Noronha was appointed in 1564 under Sebastian of Portugal as viceroy of India. Previously, he served at Ceuta in the 1540s and had been captaining at Hormuz in the 1550s. He was the illegitimate son of João de Noronha and nephew of viceroy Afonso de Noronha (1550–1554). Antão de Noronha was also the Viceroy of Portuguese India between 3 September 1564 and September 1568. He captured Mangalore and built a fort there in 1568. He died in 1569 on board in his voyage back to Portugal.

input: Assembly theory was developed by Lee Cronin and his colleagues as a framework for quantifying the complexity of molecules and objects by determining the minimum number of steps required to build them from fundamental components. Central to this theory is the assembly index, a measurable metric that captures how structurally complex a given molecule is. Cronin's team argues that this approach is empirically testable and has potential applications in examining selection mechanisms, evolutionary dynamics, and the identification of biosignatures within astrobiology. However, the method's practical utility has been met with skepticism from other researchers in the field.
target: Assembly theory is a framework developed to quantify the complexity of molecules and objects by assessing the minimal number of steps required to assemble them from fundamental building blocks. Proposed by chemist Lee Cronin and his team, the theory assigns an assembly index to molecules, which serves as a measurable indicator of their structural complexity. Cronin and colleagues argue that this approach allows for experimental verification and has applications in understanding selection processes, evolution, and the identification of biosignatures in astrobiology. However, the usefulness of the approach has been disputed.

input: A tunneling protocol is a form of network communication that allows data to be moved between separate networks. For instance, these protocols make it possible for sensitive private data to travel across public networks like the Internet, or they enable an incompatible network protocol to operate over another through a technique known as encapsulation. Since tunneling wraps traffic in a different format—often including encryption—it can conceal the nature of the traffic moving through the tunnel. Tunneling protocols function by using a packet's payload portion to carry the packets that deliver the intended service. While tunneling relies on layered protocol structures resembling the OSI and TCP/IP models, it typically breaks from standard layering rules by using the payload to deliver services that are not normally available at that network layer. In most cases, the transport protocol runs at the same layer or a higher layer within the layered structure than the service protocol it is transporting.
target: In computer networks, a tunneling protocol is a communication protocol that allows for the movement of data from one network to another. They can, for example, allow private communications to be sent across a public network (such as the Internet), or for one network protocol to be carried over an incompatible network, through a process called encapsulation. Because tunneling involves repackaging the traffic data into a different form, perhaps with encryption as standard, it can hide the nature of the traffic that is run through a tunnel. Tunneling protocols work by using the data portion of a packet (the payload) to carry the packets that actually provide the service. Tunneling uses a layered protocol model such as those of the OSI or TCP/IP protocol suite, but usually violates the layering when using the payload to carry a service not normally provided by the network. Typically, the delivery protocol operates at an equal or higher level in the layered model than the payload protocol.

input: Devo, an American new wave band, released Smooth Noodle Maps (written as smoothnoodlemaps) as their eighth studio album in June 1990. This was their final record with Enigma Records. Recording took place at Master Control Studios in Burbank, California across three months, from October 1989 through January 1990. The album marked Devo's last full-length studio release before 2010's Something for Everybody, and it was also the final studio album to include David Kendrick as the drummer. The single "Post Post-Modern Man" peaked at No. 7 on the Billboard Modern Rock Tracks chart during the week of August 11, 1990, and reached No. 26 on Billboard's Hot Dance/Club Play chart during the week of September 29, 1990.

Liam Devally (1933–9 April 2018), born in Cahir, County Tipperary, Ireland, died in Dublin. An Irish radio and television presenter and singer who later became a barrister and judge, Devally was the son of a Garda officer. When he was a child, his family relocated to Mullingar, County Westmeath. He received a scholarship to study at St Enda's College in Galway.

Throughout his broadcasting career, Devally hosted numerous programmes across Ireland. He worked as a radio presenter on RTÉ Radio 1 and became familiar to Irish audiences between 1972 and 1979, a period during which he commentated on the Eurovision Song Contest for RTÉ Radio. His recordings included My Lagan Love and Eileen Aroon. In 1959, he featured on the Ed Sullivan Show in America, and in 1966, he portrayed the Irish revolutionary Eamon Ceant in the dramatisation Insurrection.

Devally married Mairead Connaghton, whom he met while working at RTÉ, and the couple settled in Blackrock, County Dublin. He subsequently entered the legal profession as a barrister and served as a Circuit Court judge from 1991 until his retirement. He died in Dublin at the age of 85 and was buried in Kilmacanogue Cemetery, County Wicklow.

input: Mary Lee Burrows, born Mary Lee McCauley on August 27, 1932, and died on October 23, 2018, was an American politician who served in the Oregon House of Representatives. She attended Northwest Christian University and previously worked as a secretary for the California Republican Assembly. Additionally, Burrows served as the chairperson for Lane County's campaign efforts for Senator Bob Packwood during the 1967 election and for Governor Tom McCall during the 1970 election.
target: Mary Lee Burrows (née McCauley; August 27, 1932 - October 23, 2018) was an American politician who was a member of the Oregon House of Representatives. She is an alumnus of Northwest Christian University and former secretary for the California Republican Assembly. input: Lokomby is a commune and settlement located in Madagascar, specifically within the Manakara district of the Fitovinany region. According to the 2001 commune census, the population was estimated at around 15,000 people. The town has both primary and lower secondary schools. The main source of livelihood is agriculture, which employs approximately 95% of the commune's residents. The principal crops are coffee and rice, while cloves, lychee, and cassava are also significant products. The remaining 5% of the population is employed in the service sector.
target: Lokomby is a town and commune in Madagascar. It belongs to the district of Manakara, which is a part of Fitovinany. The population of the commune was estimated to be approximately 15,000 in 2001 commune census. Primary and junior level secondary education are available in town. The majority 95% of the population of the commune are farmers. The most important crops are coffee and rice, while other important agricultural products are cloves, lychee and cassava. Services provide employment for 5% of the population.

input: Born on 24 January 1988, Sylwester Janiszewski is a retired Polish professional cyclist who competed for four different teams across two separate stints in professional racing: 2008-2013 and 2015-2021. After winning the 2012 Memoriał Henryka Łasaka, he returned a positive test for Androstenedione, which led to his suspension and the stripping of that victory. His triumph at the Coupe des Carpathes, achieved the following day, was not subject to the same fate and remained his.
target: Sylwester Janiszewski (born 24 January 1988) is a Polish former racing cyclist, who rode professionally for four teams between 2008 and 2013, and 2015 and 2021. input: This topical guide and overview provides details on Rajasthan: Situated in northwestern India, Rajasthan holds the distinction of being the largest state in the Republic of India by area. input: DELTA, which stands for DEscription Language for TAxonomy, is a data format employed in taxonomic research to document the characteristics of organisms. Built with automated processing in mind, it enables the creation of identification keys, diagnostic descriptions, and similar outputs. The format has become widely accepted as a standard, and numerous software applications have been developed to serve a range of taxonomic needs. It was developed by CSIRO's Australian Division of Entomology between 1971 and 2000, with Dr. Michael J. Dallwitz playing a central role in its creation. More recently, the Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) ported the DELTA software to Java, allowing it to run in Java environments and across multiple operating systems. The software is now available for download from the ALA website.
target: DELTA (DEscription Language for TAxonomy) is a data format used in taxonomy for recording descriptions of living things. It is designed for computer processing, allowing the generation of identification keys, diagnosis, etc. It is widely accepted as a standard and many programs using this format are available for various taxonomic tasks. It was devised by the CSIRO Australian Division of Entomology in 1971 to 2000, with a notable part taken by Dr. Michael J. Dallwitz. More recently, the Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) rewrote the DELTA software in Java so it can run in a Java environment and across multiple operating systems. The software package can now be found at and downloaded from the ALA site.

input: Constructed in 1888, the Rush County Courthouse is situated at 715 Elm St. in La Crosse, Kansas. The structure was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1972 and functions as the courthouse for Rush County. This two-story edifice features brick construction in common bond pattern and includes a full basement. A bond issue valued at $20,000, approved by voters on July 10, 1888, financed the building's construction.
target: The Rush County Courthouse in La Crosse, Kansas was built in 1888. Located at 715 Elm St., it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972. It serves Rush County, Kansas. It is a two-story brick building, with brick laid in common bond, on a full basement. It was funded by a $20,000 bond issue voted upon on July 10, 1888.

Kothagudem Assembly constituency is a legislative assembly constituency located in Telangana, India. It falls within Bhadradri Kothagudem district and encompasses the municipalities of Kothagudem and Palwancha, as well as part of the Khammam Lok Sabha constituency.

The constituency is currently represented by Jalagam Venkat Rao, who is serving his second term. He obtained his seat after it was discovered that his opponent, Vanama Venkateshwar Rao of the Congress party, had filed a false affidavit during the 2018 Telangana assembly elections. Jalagam Venkat Rao subsequently brought the case before the High Court, which ruled in his favor in 2023. Consequently, in 2023 the High Court officially declared Jalagam Venkat Rao the MLA of this constituency, about five months prior to the next Telangana assembly elections.

input: Jane Fenmore Barnes, an American actress who worked in both film and theatre, was born on August 17, 1910, and died on March 20, 1998. She rose to prominence during the 1930s, having originally trained to become a concert pianist before ultimately deciding to pursue acting. Prior to entering the film industry, she built experience through stage performances, radio dramas, and modeling. She went on to sign with Fox Studios, where between 1934 and 1937 she took on a variety of notable and supporting roles in film. Following this period, she shifted her focus to the stage in order to refine her abilities as an actress, and in August 1937 she wed fellow actor Carlyle Moore Jr. After failing to achieve the success she had hoped for on Broadway in New York, she changed direction and became a newspaper columnist, moving back and forth between Massachusetts and Hollywood on several occasions. In her later years, she settled in Victorville, California, where she became involved with her local library organization, a reflection of her lifelong love of reading.
target: Jane Fenmore Barnes (August 17, 1910 – March 20, 1998) was an American film and theatre actress during the 1930s. She originally studied to become a concert pianist before deciding to become an actress instead, spending several years on the theatre circuit along with radio dramas and modeling before becoming a film star for Fox Studios. Cast in multiple major and minor film roles from 1934 through 1937, she then returned to theatre work to hone her acting skills before marrying actor Carlyle Moore Jr. in August 1937. When her theatre plans in New York on Broadway did not work out, she became a columnist for multiple papers, moving several times back to Massachusetts and then Hollywood. In her later years, she settled in Victorville, California, and became a part of her local library group to support her love of books.

input: Born on 26 December 1985, Thomas Christopher Smith is a retired English cricketer who represented Lancashire County Cricket Club. He previously participated in the England Academy. During 2008, he was loaned to Leicestershire after struggling to secure a place in Lancashire's senior squad. As an all-rounder, he bowls right-arm medium pace and bats left-handed. Beginning in the 2009 season, Smith was moved up to opening the batting, a position he held having previously batted lower down the order, where he established himself as a regular. In 2011—when Lancashire captured their first County Championship title since 1950—Smith made history by becoming the first Lancashire batsman to score a century and take four wickets in a single one-day match. During 2011/12, Smith appeared for the Matabeleland Tuskers as a foreign player in Zimbabwe's domestic twenty20 tournament.

input: Baron Vladimir Ivanovich Staël von Holstein (Russian: Владимир Иванович Сталь фон Гольштейн; 29 June 1853 – 21 September 1921) served as a lieutenant general in the Imperial Russian Army. The majority of his military career was spent assigned to the staff of the Petersburg Military District. From 1908 onward, he served as vice-commandant of the Peter and Paul Fortress, a post he held at the time of the February Revolution, during which he was in command of the fortress.
target: Baron Vladimir Ivanovich Staël von Holstein (Russian: Владимир Иванович Сталь фон Гольштейн; 29 June 1853 – 21 September 1921) was a Russian imperial army officer who reached the rank of lieutenant general. He spent most of his career on the staff of the Petersburg Military District and served as vice-commandant of the Peter and Paul Fortress from 1908. He commanded the fortress during the February Revolution.

input: The Dachstein Chapel, called Dachsteinkapelle in German, stands beside the Simony Hut in the Dachstein Mountains at an elevation of 2,206 metres (7,238 ft), making it the highest place of worship in the Northern Limestone Alps. The chapel is situated within the municipality of Hallstatt, in the Gmunden district of Upper Austria, Austria. It comes under the jurisdiction of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Linz and has been listed as a protected cultural monument.
target: The Dachstein Chapel (German: Dachsteinkapelle) is located immediately next to the Simony Hut in the Dachstein Mountains. input: The Jowett Bradford was a British light van produced by Jowett Cars Ltd, a company located in Idle, near Bradford, England, from 1946 to 1953. An estate car version was additionally available between 1947 and 1953. The model was based on the pre-war Jowett Eight and was the first Jowett vehicle to re-enter production after World War II. Although straightforward in design, the Bradford appealed to post-war buyers due to its fuel economy and ease of availability.

input: Since 29 December 2020, the Republic of Ireland has been conducting an extensive mass immunisation initiative called the COVID-19 vaccination programme. This campaign was launched to address the COVID-19 pandemic affecting Ireland. The Irish vaccination effort has earned recognition as among the world's most effective programmes. Within the European Union, it achieved the highest ranking for the proportion of adults who completed their full vaccination course and also topped EU rankings for booster dose administration. By 20 February 2023, the campaign had delivered a total of 12,744,694 vaccine doses, with 4,107,865 individuals receiving at least one dose, 3,819,227 receiving two doses, and 4,817,602 receiving a booster dose.

input: Born on January 29, 1932, in Lodi, California, Maximo Yabes lost his life on February 26, 1967. A soldier in the United States Army, he received the Medal of Honor posthumously — the nation's highest military award — in recognition of his courageous actions during the Vietnam War near Phu Hoa Dong, South Vietnam. Yabes displayed remarkable bravery by using his own body to protect fellow soldiers sheltering in a bunker, moving two wounded men to safety so they could receive medical attention, and destroying an enemy machine gun position. He died as a result of wounds suffered while carrying out these acts.
target: Maximo Yabes (January 29, 1932 – February 26, 1967) born in Lodi, California, was a United States Army soldier who posthumously received the Medal of Honor — the United States' highest military decoration — for his actions near Phu Hoa Dong in South Vietnam during the Vietnam War. Yabes distinguished himself when he used his body as a shield to protect others in a bunker, moved two wounded men to a safer position where they could be given medical treatment and destroyed an enemy machine gun position before being mortally wounded.

input: Butler's dunnart, scientifically named Sminthopsis butleri, is also referred to as the Carpentarian dunnart. This small marsupial shares similar characteristics with its close relative, the Kakadu dunnart, featuring a fluffy coat that ranges in colour from brown to mouse grey on the dorsal surface, contrasting with a white ventral side. The species measures 75-88mm from head to anus, with a tail spanning 72-90mm, resulting in a combined body length of 147-178mm. Adult individuals typically weigh between 10-20g, with variation influenced by factors such as sex, habitat type, and food availability.

input: The Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (UERJ) is a leading public research university situated in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. input: The Gyrokinetic ElectroMagnetic (GEM) code is a simulation tool for gyrokinetic plasma turbulence that employs the δ f {\displaystyle \delta f} particle-in-cell method. Its primary application is investigating waves, instabilities, and nonlinear dynamics in tokamak fusion plasmas. Details regarding GEM are available on its dedicated web page. GEM exists in two variants: a flux-tube variant and a global general geometry variant. Both variants employ a field-aligned coordinate system. The code represents ions using kinetic treatment with gyro-orbit averaging, while representing electrons using drift-kinetic treatment.
target: Gyrokinetic ElectroMagnetic (GEM) is a gyrokinetic plasma turbulence simulation that uses the δ f {\displaystyle \delta f} particle-in-cell method. It is used to study waves, instabilities and nonlinear behavior of tokamak fusion plasmas. Information about GEM can be found at the GEM web page. There are two versions of GEM, one is a flux-tube version and the other one is a global general geometry version. Both versions of GEM use a field-aligned coordinate system. Ions are treated kinetically, but averaged over their gyro-orbits and electrons are treated as drift-kinetic.

input: The Pasquino Group, alternatively titled Menelaus Carrying the Body of Patroclus or Ajax Carrying the Body of Achilles, comprises marble sculptural works modeled after an original Hellenistic bronze piece from approximately 200–150 BCE. At least fifteen Roman marble reproductions of this artwork have been identified. These marble reproductions possess complicated artistic and cultural backgrounds that demonstrate the extent of makeshift "restorations" performed on damaged fragments of ancient Roman sculptures during the 16th and 17th centuries, when contemporary Italian sculptors incorporated new and frequently arbitrary, damaging additions to reconstruct missing portions of ancient works. Among the most well-known renditions of this composition, though heavily fragmented and deteriorated such that its connection is barely evident initially, stands the renowned Pasquin, which ranks among Rome's celebrated talking statues. It was erected on a base in 1501 and has remained unrestored since. A variant of the group, seemingly intended to depict additional figures from Homer's epics, exists among the Sperlonga sculptures, which were discovered in 1957.
target: The Pasquino Group (also known as Menelaus Carrying the Body of Patroclus or Ajax Carrying the Body of Achilles) is a group of marble sculptures that copy a Hellenistic bronze original, dating to ca. 200–150 BCE. At least fifteen Roman marble copies of this sculpture are known. Many of these marble copies have complex artistic and social histories that illustrate the degree to which improvisatory "restorations" were made to fragments of ancient Roman sculpture during the 16th and 17th centuries, in which contemporary Italian sculptors made original and often arbitrary and destructive additions in an effort to replace lost fragments of the ancient sculptures. One of the most famous versions of the composition, though so dismembered and battered that the relationship is scarcely recognizable at first glance, is the so-called Pasquin, one of the talking statues of Rome. It was set up on a pedestal in 1501 and remains unrestored. A version of the group, probably intended to represent other Homeric figures, is part of the Sperlonga sculptures found in 1957.

input: Pinoquio is a monotypic genus of South American cellar spiders containing only one species: Pinoquio barauna. When B. A. Huber and L. S. Carvalho first described the genus in 2019, they named it Pinocchio, drawing inspiration from the fictional character of the same name whose distinctive nose bore a resemblance to the projecting clypeus seen in P. barauna. However, this original name created a problem, as it was already in use by the harvestman genus Pinocchio Mello-Leitão, 1940 (which has since been synonymized with Bresslauius Mello-Leitão, 1935). To resolve this conflict, the genus was renamed Pinoquio in 2022, taking the Portuguese form of the name of Collodi's famous character. The genus is known to occur exclusively in Brazil.
target: Pinoquio is a monotypic genus of South American cellar spiders containing the single species, Pinoquio barauna. It was first described with the name Pinocchio by B. A. Huber & L. S. Carvalho in 2019, after Pinocchio, whose famous nose reminded the authors of the projecting clypeus in P. barauna. However, this name turned out to be a junior homonym that had been used before, for the harvestman genus Pinocchio Mello-Leitão, 1940 (now considered a synonym of Bresslauius Mello-Leitão, 1935). Therefore, the genus name was amended in 2022 to Pinoquio, which is the Portuguese spelling of the name of Collodi's famous character. This genus has only been found in Brazil.

input: A BAC One-Eleven aircraft operated by Oriental Airlines (tail number 5N-IMO) went down on 18 September 1994 while attempting to land at Aguenar – Hadj Bey Akhamok Airport in Tamanrasset, Algeria. The accident killed five people: three crew members and two passengers. The aircraft was operating as a charter flight from Tunis, Tunisia, headed to Lagos, Nigeria, carrying the Nigerian soccer team Iwuanyanwu Nationale (currently known as Heartland FC) back home after playing an away game against Espérance.
target: On 18 September 1994, an Oriental Airlines BAC One-Eleven (registration 5N-IMO) crashed during an attempted landing at Aguenar – Hadj Bey Akhamok Airport in Tamanrasset, Algeria. The crash resulted in five fatalities—two passengers and three crew members. The charter flight, traveling from Tunis, Tunisia, to Lagos, Nigeria, was arranged to return the Nigerian football team Iwuanyanwu Nationale (now Heartland FC) following an away match against Espérance.

Tunstall Healthcare, founded in 1957 and based in Doncaster, is a technology company that specializes in digital health and care services. Operating across 19 countries, the company employs approximately 3,000 people and serves 5 million connected users globally, positioning it as a major player in the telehealth market. Emil Peters serves as Chief Executive Officer.

The company's notable acquisitions include American Medical Alert Corporation (December 2011), Secuvita, a Dutch technology solutions provider with 70,000 users (2021), and BeWo Unternehmensgruppe, a German firm (2022). In January 2019, Tunstall divested Tunstall Americas to Connect America.com, a decision aligned with its strategic shift toward a technology-driven managed services model.

Tunstall collaborates with Telefónica to deliver remote patient management systems and services, enhancing its preventive care capabilities for patients with chronic conditions. In 2019, the company co-authored a report with hft, a charitable organization, which was launched in the House of Lords. The report examined the untapped potential of assistive technology in social care and received endorsement from the Voluntary Organisations Disability Group.
target: Tunstall Healthcare is a technology company established in 1957 which specialises in digital health and care services. Its head office is in Doncaster. It has around 3,000 staff in 19 countries, and 5 million connected end users worldwide. It is regarded as a key player in the telehealth market. The Chief Executive Officer is Emil Peters. It acquired American Medical Alert Corporation in December 2011. It sold Tunstall Americas to Connect America.com in January 2019 as part of its move towards a technology-enabled managed services business model. input: Nicomedia's Martyrs comprise a substantial Christian community traditionally said to have perished in the Roman settlement of Nicomedia when the Roman Empire persecuted its Christian population. Christian historical accounts maintain that numerous adherents were executed in this city during the early 300s for declining to abandon their religion or make offerings to Roman deities. These occurrences are typically linked to the concluding stage of the Diocletianic Persecution, which scholars term the Great Persecution—representing the Roman Empire's most severe campaign against Christians before Constantine the Great legalized Christianity. Byzantine sources from later periods document what is described as a particularly severe killing spree occurring on Christmas in 304 AD, in which a large assembly of Christians observing Jesus's birth celebration was allegedly executed for rejecting participation in non-Christian ritual sacrifices. Christian historical writings provide varying estimates of casualty numbers. Certain sources cite thousands of casualties, whereas later religious texts document 20,000 martyrs in Nicomedia. Contemporary historical scholars typically view the higher figures as legendary or religious embellishment rather than historically reliable numbers.
target: The Martyrs of Nicomedia refer to a large group of Christians traditionally believed to have been killed in the Roman city of Nicomedia during the persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire. According to Christian tradition, thousands of Christians were killed in the city during the early fourth century after refusing to renounce their faith or offer sacrifices to the Roman gods. The events are usually connected with the final phase of the Diocletianic Persecution, often referred to by historians as the Great Persecution, the most extensive persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire prior to the legalization of Christianity under Constantine the Great. Later Byzantine traditions describe a particularly large massacre occurring on Christmas Day in 304 AD, when a large gathering of Christians celebrating the Nativity of Jesus was reportedly killed after refusing to participate in pagan sacrificial rites. The number of victims recorded in Christian sources varies widely. Some accounts describe several thousand victims, while later liturgical texts refer to 20,000 martyrs who died in Nicomedia. Modern historians generally treat the larger number as symbolic or hagiographical rather than a precise historical count.

input: Adır Island (Turkish: Adır Adası), also called Lim Island (Armenian: Լիմ կղզի, romanized: Lim kghzi), represents the biggest island within Lake Van, situated on the lake's northeastern portion. During the Armenian genocide, more than 12,000 Armenian women and children made their way to the island across three days, while approximately a few dozen men provided defensive cover for their crossing against Hamidiye regiments. The circumstances rapidly became dire due to insufficient food supplies. An Armenian monastery, Lim Monastery, was constructed on the island over many centuries. Armenian historical sources suggest the monastery's establishment predated 884, though tradition attributes its founding to St. Gregory the Illuminator in the 4th century. By the 1300s, the site contained three churches: Surp Astvatsatsin, Surp Garabed, and Surp Kevork. In 1766, a bell tower, chapel, and parish residence were constructed. The monastery continued operations until 1918, after which it experienced continuous decline. An elaborate altar curtain from the monastery remains exceptionally well-preserved and is currently housed in the San Lazzaro Island museum in Venice.
target: Adır Island (Turkish: Adır Adası) or Lim Island (Armenian: Լիմ կղզի, romanized: Lim kghzi), is the largest island in Lake Van, located in the northeastern side of the lake. During the Armenian genocide upwards of 12,000 Armenian women and children, crossed to the isle over a period of three days while a few dozen men covered their retreat from Hamidiye regiments. The situation soon became critical because of a lack of food. Lim Monastery was built by Armenians over the centuries on the island, with Armenian sources indicating the monastery was already founded pre-884, with tradition saying that St. Gregory the Illuminator himself founded it in the 4th century. By the 14th century there were Surp Astvatsatsin, Surp Garabed and Surp Kevork churches. In 1766 the belltower, a chapel and a parish house were built. The monastery functioned until 1918, and has deteriorated ever since. The large, intricate curtain from one of the altars is preserved in very good condition at the museum of San Lazzaro Island in Venice.

input: The Kategoria e Dytë represents the third level of professional football in Albania. Called the Second Division since the 2004–05 season, it features 23 teams divided into two geographic groups. The top team in each group earns promotion to the Kategoria e Parë, and the two group champions then meet in a final that decides the overall winner of the season. At the same time, the lowest-ranked teams in each group are relegated to the Kategoria e Tretë.
target: Kategoria e Dytë is the third tier of professional football in Albania’s league system. Known as the Second Division since the 2004–05 season, it consists of 23 teams split into two geographically-based groups. The winners of each group secure promotion to Kategoria e Parë and face off in the final to determine the season’s overall champion. Meanwhile, the last positioned teams in each group are relegated to Kategoria e Tretë.

input: Brazil's president officially resides at the Palácio da Alvorada (pronounced [paˈlasju dawvoˈɾadɐ] in Portuguese). This structure stands in Brasília, the nation's capital, situated on a peninsula extending into Paranoá Lake. Oscar Niemeyer designed the building, which was constructed between 1957 and 1958 using modernist architectural principles. Since Juscelino Kubitschek, every Brazilian president has called it home. The building holds the status of a National Historic Heritage Site. The Palácio da Alvorada functions as both a presidential residence and a venue for state ceremonies. The Palácio do Planalto, however, serves as the president's office and the seat of executive power.
target: The Palácio da Alvorada (Portuguese pronunciation: [paˈlasju dawvoˈɾadɐ]) is the official residence of the president of Brazil. It is located in the national capital of Brasília, on a peninsula at the margins of Paranoá Lake. The building was designed by Oscar Niemeyer and built between 1957 and 1958 in the modernist style. It has been the residence of every Brazilian president since Juscelino Kubitschek. The building is listed as a National Historic Heritage Site. The Palácio da Alvorada is used as a residence and for official receptions. The president's workplace and center of the executive branch is the Palácio do Planalto.

UWA-001, also referred to as α-phenyl-MDMA and methylenedioxymephenidine, is a compound derived from phenethylamine that was created at the University of Western Australia. It was engineered to serve as a safer substitute for 3,4-methylenedioxy-N-methylamphetamine (MDMA) and has been studied as a possible therapy for Parkinson's disease.

Concerning its receptor binding characteristics, UWA-001 shows a 5-HT2A receptor affinity of 1.2 μM (roughly 10 times stronger than MDMA), a serotonin transporter affinity of 1.3 μM (about 4 times weaker than MDMA), a norepinephrine transporter affinity of 13.4 μM (approximately 26 times stronger than MDMA), and minimal dopamine transporter affinity (over 50 μM).

In contrast to MDMA and para-methoxyamphetamine, but like ketamine, UWA-001 enhances prepulse inhibition. From this observation, researchers determined that the compound has no psychoactive effects, though no evaluations were carried out at additional binding sites. Although UWA-001 displays cytotoxicity against the SH-SY5Y cell line at high concentrations, it is markedly less toxic than MDMA across all concentration levels tested.

Structurally, UWA-001 is related to diarylethylamines including lefetamine (a stimulant and opioid agent) and ephenidine (a dissociative anesthetic functioning as an NMDA receptor antagonist).
target: UWA-001 (also known as α-phenyl-MDMA and methylenedioxymephenidine) is a phenethylamine derivative invented at the University of Western Australia as non-toxic alternative to 3,4-methylenedioxy-N-methylamphetamine (MDMA) and researched as a potential treatment for Parkinson's disease. It has a 5-HT2A receptor affinity of 1.2 μM (~10-fold increase compared to MDMA), 1.3 μM for the serotonin transporter (~4-fold decrease compared to MDMA), 13.4 μM for the norepinephrine transporter (~26-fold increase compared to MDMA) and virtually no affinity for the dopamine transporter (>50 μM). Unlike MDMA and para-methoxyamphetamine (but similarly to ketamine), UWA-001 increases prepulse inhibition and was therefore considered to be non-psychoactive, though it was not assayed at other binding sites. It is toxic to the SH-SY5Y cell line at high concentrations, however significantly less toxic than MDMA at all concentrations tested. UWA-001 is structurally related to the diarylethylamines lefetamine (a stimulant and opioid) and the dissociative anesthetic ephenidine, which acts as a NMDA receptor antagonist.

input: Mountain Swainson-pea, also called small purple pea, refers to *Swainsona recta*, a flowering plant belonging to the Fabaceae family that is found exclusively in south-eastern mainland Australia. This perennial species grows upright or at an ascending angle and features imparipinnate foliage consisting of 5 to 13 extremely thin, linear leaflets. The plant produces racemes containing approximately 6 to over 25 purple-colored flowers.
target: Swainsona recta, commonly known as mountain Swainson-pea or small purple pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to the south-east of continental Australia. It is an erect or ascending perennial plant with imparipinnate leaves with 5 to 13 very narrowly linear leaflets, and racemes of about 6 to more than 25 purple flowers.

input: Songs of the Southern Skies is a collaborative studio album featuring Australian singer-songwriter Katie Noonan and Australian classical guitarist Karin Schaupp. Released in August 2012, the album reached number 97 on the ARIA physical albums chart and number 3 on the classical chart. It showcases classical, folk, jazz, and pop music from Australia and New Zealand. The Brisbane-recorded album features guest appearances from Iva Davies, Gurrumul, Whirimako Black, Diana Doherty, Clare Bowditch, and Chris Cheney. Noonan explained: "this project brings together my two main musical loves – classical and pop music. As an artist I love blurring the boundaries of genre and hearing musical worlds collide. This project is a wonderful opportunity for Karin and I to do exactly that!" The album was toured throughout 2013. At the 2012 ARIA Music Awards, Songs of the Southern Skies received nominations for 'Best Adult Contemporary' album (losing to The Ol' Razzle Dazzle by Missy Higgins) and 'Best Independent Release' (losing to Prisoner by The Jezabels).

input: Jimma Aba Jifar Football Club (ጅማ አባ ጅፋር in Amharic; Jimmaa Abbaa Jifaar in Afaan Oromo) is a professional soccer team headquartered in Jimma, Ethiopia. input: American new wave band Devo released their eighth studio album, Smooth Noodle Maps (stylized as smoothnoodlemaps), in June 1990. The album served as their last release with Enigma Records and was recorded over a three-month period at Master Control Studios in Burbank, California, between October 1989 and January 1990. It would remain Devo's final full-length studio effort until Something for Everybody arrived in 2010, and it also marked the last studio album to feature drummer David Kendrick. The single "Post Post-Modern Man" climbed to No. 7 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart for the week of August 11, 1990, and later reached No. 26 on Billboard's Hot Dance/Club Play chart for the week of September 29, 1990.
target: Smooth Noodle Maps (stylized as smoothnoodlemaps) is the eighth studio album by the American new wave band Devo. It was originally released in June 1990 and would be their last album released through Enigma. The album was recorded over a period of three months between October 1989 and January 1990, at Master Control Studios, in Burbank, California. Smooth Noodle Maps was Devo's last full-length studio album until the release of Something for Everybody in 2010, as well as the last Devo studio album to feature David Kendrick on drums. "Post Post-Modern Man" hit No. 7 on the Billboard Modern Rock Tracks chart for the week of August 11, 1990 and No. 26 on Billboard's Hot Dance/Club Play chart for the week of September 29, 1990.

input: Hi-Q was a Romanian pop group that was established in 1996 in Braşov. The group's founding members were Mihai Sturzu, Florin Grozea, and Dana Nălbaru. Libertatea recognized Hi-Q as among Romania's most prominent musical acts, and the band also ran its own television program on a national channel. Dana Nălbaru departed from the group in 2003 to launch a solo career, but rejoined in October 2010. The band announced their dissolution on 31 July 2014 during a news magazine program hosted by Teo Trandafir.
target: Hi-Q was a Romanian pop group, founded in 1996 in Braşov. The original group consisted of Mihai Sturzu, Florin Grozea, and Dana Nălbaru. Described by Libertatea as one of the best-known musical groups in Romania, Hi-Q also hosted its own TV show on national television. Dana Nălbaru left the group in 2003 to pursue a solo career and returned in October 2010. On 31 July 2014, on a news magazine show presented by Teo Trandafir, the band split.

input: The European Broadcasting Union (EBU) produces the Eurovision Debate, a live televised event featuring the leading political contenders (known as "Spitzenkandidaten") seeking the position of European Commission President. Broadcast throughout Europe using the Eurovision network and organized by the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium, this debate serves to strengthen public service media's contribution to democracy. By enhancing citizen awareness and promoting electoral engagement, the debate facilitates the democratic process.
target: The Eurovision Debate is a live televised debate between the lead political candidates ("Spitzenkandidaten") running to be the next President of the European Commission. Produced by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) and broadcast across Europe via the Eurovision network, the debate is hosted by the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium. The aim of the debate is to help public service media play their role in the democratic process by helping to better inform citizens and encouraging participation in the elections.

input: This topical guide and overview offers information about Rajasthan: Located in northwestern India, Rajasthan is notable for being the largest state in the Republic of India by area. Much of the expansive and harsh Thar Desert—commonly called the Great Indian Desert—lies within the state, stretching along the Sutlej-Indus river valley on its western border with Pakistan. Elsewhere, Rajasthan shares borders with Gujarat (to the southwest), Madhya Pradesh (to the southeast), Uttar Pradesh and Haryana (to the northeast), and Punjab (to the north). Encompassing a total area of 342,239 square kilometres (132,139 square miles), Rajasthan makes up 10.4% of India's total land area.

Born in Zürich on 23 February 1838, Swiss literary historian Ludwig Hirzel died on 1 June 1897. His father, Ludwig Hirzel (1801–1841), held a professorship in theology at the University of Zürich. After obtaining his doctorate from the University of Zürich in 1862, Hirzel worked as a secondary educator, first in Frauenfeld (1862) and later at the Aarau cantonal school (1866). Starting in 1874, he held the position of professor of German language and literature at the University of Berne until his death in 1897.

Hirzel's scholarly contributions included studies of prominent literary figures such as Goethe, Schiller, and Wieland. He is particularly noted for producing authoritative editions of Albrecht von Haller's poetry (1882) and journals (1883). Additionally, he wrote an essay addressing Swiss mathematician Conrad Dasypodius and edited two works by Wieland: Geschichte der Gelehrtheit (History of the Scholars) and Beziehungen zu den deutschen Romantikern (Connections to the German Romanticists).
target: Ludwig Hirzel (23 February 1838 – 1 June 1897) was a Swiss literary historian born in Zürich. His father, also named Ludwig Hirzel (1801–1841) was a professor of theology at the University of Zürich. In 1862 he earned his doctorate from the University of Zürich. Afterwards he served as a secondary school teacher in Frauenfeld (1862) and at the cantonal school in Aarau (1866). In 1874 he became a professor of German language and literature at the University of Berne, a position he maintained until his death in 1897. Among Hirzel's literary output were books on famous writers such as Goethe, Schiller and Wieland. He was the author of acclaimed editions of Albrecht von Haller's poetry (1882) and diaries (1883). He also penned an essay on Swiss mathematician Conrad Dasypodius, and published editions of Wieland's Geschichte der Gelehrtheit (History of the Scholars) and Beziehungen zu den deutschen Romantikern (Connections to the German Romanticists).

input: The Comarca de los Montes de Toledo is a comarca situated in the southern portion of Toledo Province in Spain. While administratively part of Toledo Province, the natural boundaries of this comarca extend into several municipalities located in Ciudad Real Province. The comarca derives its name from the Montes de Toledo mountain range. Historically, like many mountainous rural regions throughout central Spain, the area was predominantly characterized by livestock herding, supplemented by modest honey production. In recent times, however, the comarca has experienced significant population decline due to economic diversification in the region.
target: Montes de Toledo Comarca (Spanish: Comarca de los Montes de Toledo) is a comarca located at the southern end of the province of Toledo, Spain. The natural comarca includes some municipal terms in Ciudad Real Province. It is named after the Montes de Toledo mountain system. and, like other mountainous rural areas in central Spain, this comarca has been traditionally a place of cattle rearers, with some honey production as well. Nowadays the comarca has suffered heavy depopulation as the economy has diversified.

input: The Rush County Courthouse, built in 1888, stands at 715 Elm St. in La Crosse, Kansas. In 1972, it was added to the National Register of Historic Places and continues to serve as the courthouse for Rush County. The two-story building is constructed of brick in a common bond pattern and has a full basement. Its construction was funded by a $20,000 bond measure that voters approved on July 10, 1888.
target: The Rush County Courthouse in La Crosse, Kansas was built in 1888. Located at 715 Elm St., it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972. It serves Rush County, Kansas. It is a two-story brick building, with brick laid in common bond, on a full basement. It was funded by a $20,000 bond issue voted upon on July 10, 1888.

input: The Langenberg (German pronunciation: [ˈlaŋənbɛʁk]) is a long chalk mountain situated between the town of Göttingerode to the south and Harlingerode to the north. It lies in Bad Harzburg, a spa town in Lower Saxony, Germany, within the Goslar district. The site is of major geological importance on a national level for two main reasons: the clearly visible Northern Harz Boundary Fault, which can be observed in the Langenberg chalk quarry, and the 1998 discovery of Europasaurus fossils in that same quarry.
target: The Langenberg (German pronunciation: [ˈlaŋənbɛʁk] ) is an elongated chalk hill north of Göttingerode and south of Harlingerode in the spa town of Bad Harzburg in Goslar district, in the German state of Lower Saxony. Due to its obvious display of the Northern Harz Boundary Fault in the Langenberg chalk quarry and the discovery of the Europasaurus in 1998 in said quarry, this mountain has gained national geological relevance.

input: Active transport of solutes across cell membranes occurs through solute pumping, a process that enables molecules to cross the lipid bilayer despite barriers such as concentration gradients or polarity that would otherwise prevent passage. This mechanism involves protein channels that facilitate molecular entry into cells. Solute pumping differs from diffusion, which operates passively without requiring cellular energy. Instead, solute pumping is an active process that depends on ATP energy to alter the protein channel's configuration, thereby permitting the passage of molecules that cannot traverse the membrane through passive means alone.
target: Solute pumping is a form of active transport of a solute through a cell membrane. Solute pumping allows a molecule that cannot regularly cross the lipid bilayer (because of concentration gradient, polarity, or other reasons) to enter the cell by way of a protein channel. Unlike diffusion (a form of passive transport), solute pumping requires energy (provided by ATP) to change the shape of the protein channel to allow the molecule to pass through, which is why it is an active transport mechanism.

input: Thomas Christopher Smith, born on 26 December 1985, is a retired English cricketer who played for Lancashire County Cricket Club and previously represented the England Academy. After finding it difficult to break into Lancashire's first team, he was loaned to Leicestershire during 2008. An all-rounder by nature, Smith bowls right-arm medium pace and bats left-handed. From the 2009 season onwards, he was promoted to opening the batting, having previously occupied a lower position in the order, and went on to cement his place as a regular starter. In 2011, the year Lancashire won their first County Championship since 1950, Smith etched his name into the club's history books by becoming the first Lancashire batsman to hit a century and claim four wickets in the same one-day match. During the 2011/12 season, he featured for the Matabeleland Tuskers as an overseas player in Zimbabwe's domestic Twenty20 competition.
target: Thomas Christopher Smith (born 26 December 1985) is a former English cricketer who played for Lancashire County Cricket Club. He had also been a member of the England Academy team. input: Baron Vladimir Ivanovich Staël von Holstein (Russian: Владимир Иванович Сталь фон Гольштейн; 29 June 1853 – 21 September 1921) was a lieutenant general in the Imperial Russian Army. He spent most of his military career attached to the staff of the Petersburg Military District. Beginning in 1908, he held the position of vice-commandant of the Peter and Paul Fortress, a role he occupied during the February Revolution, when he commanded the fortress.
target: Baron Vladimir Ivanovich Staël von Holstein (Russian: Владимир Иванович Сталь фон Гольштейн; 29 June 1853 – 21 September 1921) was a Russian imperial army officer who reached the rank of lieutenant general. He spent most of his career on the staff of the Petersburg Military District and served as vice-commandant of the Peter and Paul Fortress from 1908. He commanded the fortress during the February Revolution.

input: The Jowett Bradford was a British light van manufactured by Jowett Cars Ltd, a company based in Idle, near Bradford, England, from 1946 until 1953. An estate car variant was also offered between 1947 and 1953. The model derived from the pre-war Jowett Eight and was the first Jowett vehicle to return to production following World War II. Though simple in design, the Bradford attracted post-war buyers thanks to its fuel efficiency and ready availability.
target: The Jowett Bradford was a British light van produced from 1946 to 1953 by Jowett Cars Ltd of Idle, near Bradford, England. It was also available as an estate car from 1947 to 1953. The vehicle was based on the pre-war Jowett Eight and was the first Jowett to be re-introduced after the Second World War. Although it was very basic, the Bradford's economy and availability appealed to the post-war market.

input: The genus Zeora comprises crustose lichens belonging to the family Lecanoraceae. Members of this genus typically develop yellowish or yellow-green crusty formations with a powdery or granular appearance. While they predominantly inhabit bark and wood surfaces, certain species can also be found on rocky substrates. A large proportion of specimens lack fruiting bodies, meaning they generally appear as expanding colonies without conspicuous reproductive structures. With a nearly worldwide distribution, molecular genetic analysis has validated the restoration of Zeora as a separate genus for a cluster of taxa previously classified within Lecanora. These species are further unified by their shared production of comparable secondary metabolites characteristic of lichens, notably usnic acid and zeorin.
target: Zeora is a genus of crustose lichens in the family Lecanoraceae. Species in Zeora usually form yellowish to yellow-green crusts that may look powdery or granular, most often on bark and wood, though some also grow on rock. Many specimens are sterile, so they are often encountered as spreading patches without obvious fruiting bodies. The genus is almost cosmopolitan, and DNA-based studies have supported reviving Zeora for a distinct group of species once placed in Lecanora that also share similar secondary metabolites (lichen products), commonly including usnic acid and zeorin.

input: Killing 'em Softly, a 1982 Canadian thriller helmed by director Max Fischer and featuring Irene Cara, George Segal, Clark Johnson, and Nicholas Campbell, is primarily remembered for significant production difficulties. These complications resulted in the film becoming among the earliest Canadian movies to bypass theatrical release in favor of direct-to-video distribution, and sparked a legal dispute regarding production financing that remained unresolved until 1995. Adapted from Laird Koenig's novel The Neighbor, the narrative follows a woman whose boyfriend has been murdered; she subsequently develops romantic feelings for the man responsible for his death. input: A Carolina porch, alternatively called a rain porch, represents a distinctive indigenous porch design characteristic of the Southeastern United States. Many architectural historians attribute its origins to the Carolina coastline, which inspired its alternate name. The rain porch's distinctive feature is an expansive roof that projects significantly past the porch deck's perimeter, held up by independent vertical supports anchored at ground level rather than on the porch deck itself. This configuration provides weather protection for the porch deck and maintains substantial shade coverage throughout much of the day. While typically found on historic vernacular dwellings, rain porches were eventually incorporated into the grand porticoes of certain Greek Revival estates, including Rosemount and Kirkwood. In particularly rainy regions, such as Alabama's Eastern Shore of Mobile Bay, this design became even more pronounced. In those areas, roof overhangs frequently extended 3 to 6 feet (0.91 to 1.83 m) beyond the porch deck, effectively creating a two-level porch structure.
target: A rain porch, also commonly known as a Carolina porch, is a type of indigenous porch form found in the Southeastern United States. Some architectural scholars believe it to have originated along the coast of the Carolinas, hence the colloquial name. The defining characteristic of the rain porch is a roof that extends far beyond the edge of the porch deck and is supported with freestanding supports that rise directly from ground level, rather than the floor of the porch deck. This protects the porch deck from exposure to the elements and also leaves it well shaded from the sun most of the time. Most commonly seen on historic folk houses, the rain porch also came to be adapted to the monumental porticoes of some Greek Revival mansions, such as Rosemount and Kirkwood. The overhang became especially exaggerated in some areas with copious amounts of rainfall, such as the Eastern Shore of Mobile Bay in Alabama. Here the roof overhang ranged between 3 and 6 feet (0.91 and 1.83 m) beyond the porch deck, in effect creating a lower and upper porch.

input: Maximo Yabes was born on January 29, 1932, in Lodi, California, and died on February 26, 1967. As a soldier in the United States Army, he was posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor — the highest military honor in the nation — for his brave conduct during the Vietnam War near Phu Hoa Dong, South Vietnam. Yabes showed extraordinary courage by shielding fellow soldiers in a bunker with his own body, carrying two wounded men to safety so they could get medical care, and taking out an enemy machine gun position. He died from wounds he sustained while performing these actions.
target: Maximo Yabes (January 29, 1932 – February 26, 1967) born in Lodi, California, was a United States Army soldier who posthumously received the Medal of Honor — the United States' highest military decoration — for his actions near Phu Hoa Dong in South Vietnam during the Vietnam War. Yabes distinguished himself when he used his body as a shield to protect others in a bunker, moved two wounded men to a safer position where they could be given medical treatment and destroyed an enemy machine gun position before being mortally wounded.

input: The Constantin Diaconovici Loga National College (Colegiul Național Constantin Diaconovici Loga in Romanian) is a secondary educational institution situated at 16 C. D. Loga Street in Caransebeș, Romania. The institution's history extends back to 1582, when historical records document the existence of a teacher preparation school operating in Caransebeș. Following an 1871 decision by Ioan Popasu, the Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Caransebeș, the institution became known as the Diocesan Pedagogical Institute. The original curriculum spanned three years, though this was expanded to four years by 1895. The addition of four junior grades occurred in 1919, coinciding with Transylvania's integration with Romania. The communist government that took power in 1948 removed the school's pedagogical character, but this educational focus was reinstated in 1969. The main school building, which opened in 1899, holds the designation of a historic monument under the protection of Romania's Ministry of Culture and Religious Affairs. Construction on the upper section commenced in 1924 and concluded in 1956.
target: Constantin Diaconovici Loga National College (Romanian: Colegiul Național Constantin Diaconovici Loga) is a high school located at 16 C. D. Loga Street, Caransebeș, Romania. The school traces its origins to 1582, when a document mentions a teacher training school in Caransebeș. In 1871, Ioan Popasu, the Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Caransebeș, named it the Diocesan Pedagogical Institute. Its program lasted three years, extended to four in 1895.
