input: The Chapel of Saint Catherine, also known as the Church of Saint Catherine (Ecclesia Sanctae Catharinae in Latin; كنيسة القديسة كترينا in Arabic; כנסיית קתרינה הקדושה in Hebrew), is a Roman Catholic place of worship situated next to the northern side of the Basilica of the Nativity in Bethlehem, Palestinian territory in the West Bank. The building functions both as a parish church and a Franciscan monastery. Beneath the structure lies a system of underground caverns. The Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem oversees its administration, it observes the Roman Rite tradition, and since 2012 it has been designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site under the "Birthplace of Jesus" World Heritage designation.
target: The Church of Saint Catherine or Chapel of Saint Catherine (Latin: Ecclesia Sanctae Catharinae, Arabic: كنيسة القديسة كترينا, Hebrew: כנסיית קתרינה הקדושה) is a Catholic religious building located adjacent to the northern part of the Basilica of the Nativity in Bethlehem in the West Bank, Palestine. It works as a parish church and Franciscan monastery. There is a complex of caves underneath the church. It is administered by the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem, follows the Roman Rite, and is included in the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2012 as part of the "Birthplace of Jesus" World Heritage Site.

input: Bassline, also known as bassline house, 4x4, or niche, is an electronic dance music style that emerged in South Yorkshire during the early 2000s. The genre features a characteristic four-on-the-floor rhythm with a speed of approximately 135–142 beats per minute and prominent bass sounds reminiscent of speed garage, combined with fragmented vocal samples from R&B and pop tracks, all presented with a pop-oriented sensibility. In the genre's formative period, Sheffield's Niche Nightclub served as the most influential venue in the bassline scene until it became the subject of public controversy following a police operation that led to its permanent closure in 2005.
target: Bassline (sometimes referred to as bassline house or 4x4 or niche) is a genre of electronic dance music that originated in South Yorkshire in the early 2000s. Stylistically it comprises a four-to-the-floor beat with a tempo of around 135–142 beats per minute and a heavy bass, similar to speed garage, with chopped up R&B and Pop vocal samples and a pop music aesthetic. Particularly in the scene's early days, the most prominent bassline club was Sheffield's Niche Nightclub, which became the centre of controversy due to a police raid which resulted in the club's closure in 2005.

input: The Gyrokinetic ElectroMagnetic (GEM) code is a simulation tool for gyrokinetic plasma turbulence that utilizes the δ f {\displaystyle \delta f} particle-in-cell approach. Its main purpose is the study of waves, instabilities, and nonlinear dynamics within tokamak fusion plasmas. Further information about GEM can be found on its dedicated web page. GEM comes in two versions: a flux-tube version and a global general geometry version. Both versions make use of a field-aligned coordinate system. The code treats ions kinetically with gyro-orbit averaging, while treating electrons using a drift-kinetic approach.
target: Gyrokinetic ElectroMagnetic (GEM) is a gyrokinetic plasma turbulence simulation that uses the δ f {\displaystyle \delta f} particle-in-cell method. It is used to study waves, instabilities and nonlinear behavior of tokamak fusion plasmas. Information about GEM can be found at the GEM web page. There are two versions of GEM, one is a flux-tube version and the other one is a global general geometry version. Both versions of GEM use a field-aligned coordinate system. Ions are treated kinetically, but averaged over their gyro-orbits and electrons are treated as drift-kinetic.

input: In Seoul, South Korea, SKY represents an informal collective designation for three of the region's most academically rigorous and highly regarded institutions: Seoul National University, Korea University, and Yonsei University. The acronym has gained widespread recognition throughout South Korean society, appearing regularly in media outlets and being adopted by the universities themselves. Gaining entrance to any of these three universities is commonly regarded as a crucial factor in determining one's future career prospects and standing within Korean society. The name SKY is also meant to evoke the extreme selectivity of these institutions, suggesting that admission requires exceptional achievement (comparable to reaching for the sky).
target: SKY is an unofficial grouping and acronym for the three most prestigious and academically competitive universities located in Seoul, South Korea. It consists of Seoul National University, Korea University, and Yonsei University. The term is widely used in South Korea, both in the media and by the universities themselves. Being admitted to one of the SKY universities is frequently seen as important to one's career and social position in the country. The acronym also implies that the universities are extremely difficult to get into (i.e., students are reaching for the sky).

input: The Pasquino Group, also known as Menelaus Carrying the Body of Patroclus or Ajax Carrying the Body of Achilles, consists of marble sculptures based on an original Hellenistic bronze work dating to around 200–150 BCE. At least fifteen Roman marble copies of this piece have been identified. These copies have complex artistic and cultural histories that highlight the degree of improvised "restorations" carried out on damaged fragments of ancient Roman sculptures during the 16th and 17th centuries, when Italian sculptors of the time added new and often arbitrary, harmful elements to rebuild missing parts of ancient works. One of the most famous versions of this composition, though so heavily fragmented and worn that its subject matter is barely recognizable at first glance, is the well-known Pasquin, one of Rome's celebrated talking statues. It was placed on a pedestal in 1501 and has never been restored. A variation of the group, apparently meant to portray additional figures from Homer's epics, can be found among the Sperlonga sculptures, which were unearthed in 1957.
target: The Pasquino Group (also known as Menelaus Carrying the Body of Patroclus or Ajax Carrying the Body of Achilles) is a group of marble sculptures that copy a Hellenistic bronze original, dating to ca. 200–150 BCE. At least fifteen Roman marble copies of this sculpture are known. Many of these marble copies have complex artistic and social histories that illustrate the degree to which improvisatory "restorations" were made to fragments of ancient Roman sculpture during the 16th and 17th centuries, in which contemporary Italian sculptors made original and often arbitrary and destructive additions in an effort to replace lost fragments of the ancient sculptures. One of the most famous versions of the composition, though so dismembered and battered that the relationship is scarcely recognizable at first glance, is the so-called Pasquin, one of the talking statues of Rome. It was set up on a pedestal in 1501 and remains unrestored. A version of the group, probably intended to represent other Homeric figures, is part of the Sperlonga sculptures found in 1957.

input: Pinoquio is a monotypic genus of South American cellar spiders that includes just a single species: Pinoquio barauna. When B. A. Huber and L. S. Carvalho originally described the genus in 2019, they gave it the name Pinocchio, inspired by the fictional character of that name whose signature nose resembled the protruding clypeus found in P. barauna. This initial name, however, posed a problem because it was already taken by the harvestman genus Pinocchio Mello-Leitão, 1940 (which has since been synonymized with Bresslauius Mello-Leitão, 1935). To settle this conflict, the genus was renamed Pinoquio in 2022, adopting the Portuguese version of the name of Collodi's celebrated character. The genus is found only in Brazil.
target: Pinoquio is a monotypic genus of South American cellar spiders containing the single species, Pinoquio barauna. It was first described with the name Pinocchio by B. A. Huber & L. S. input: McKayla Rose Maroney, born on December 9, 1995, is a retired American artistic gymnast. As part of the Fierce Five — the U.S. women's gymnastics team that captured gold in the team event at the 2012 Summer Olympics — she also earned a silver medal in the individual vault competition at those same Games. At the 2011 World Championships, she helped the American team secure the gold medal and claimed the vault title on her own. She later made history at the 2013 World Championships, becoming the first American female gymnast to successfully defend a World Championship vault title. Earlier in her career, she captured three gold medals at the 2010 Pan American Championships. A widely circulated Internet meme came from a photograph taken after her silver medal vault performance at the 2012 Summer Olympics, in which Maroney displayed an obvious "not impressed" expression. After her final competitive appearance at the 2013 World Championships, Maroney officially announced her retirement from gymnastics in 2016.
target: McKayla Rose Maroney (born December 9, 1995) is an American former artistic gymnast. She was a member of the American women's gymnastics team, dubbed the Fierce Five, that won a gold medal in the team competition at the 2012 Summer Olympics. There, she also won an individual silver medal on the vault. Maroney was also a member of the gold-winning American team at the 2011 World Championships, where she also won the vault title. She then became the first U.S. female gymnast to defend a World Championship vault title at the 2013 World Championships. Earlier in her career, she won three gold medals at the 2010 Pan American Championships. A photograph of Maroney with a "not impressed" expression, taken after winning the vault silver medal at the 2012 Summer Olympics, became an Internet meme. In 2016, she retired from gymnastics after not competing since the 2013 World Championships.

input: In 1564, King Sebastian of Portugal appointed D. Antão de Noronha to the position of viceroy of India. His earlier career included a posting at Ceuta during the 1540s and a captaincy at Hormuz in the 1550s. Born as the illegitimate child of João de Noronha, he was also the nephew of former viceroy Afonso de Noronha, who served from 1550 to 1554. Antão de Noronha governed Portuguese India from 3 September 1564 until September 1568. During his tenure, he conquered Mangalore and established a fort there in 1568. He passed away in 1569 while returning to Portugal by sea.
target: D. Antão de Noronha was appointed in 1564 under Sebastian of Portugal as viceroy of India. Previously, he served at Ceuta in the 1540s and had been captaining at Hormuz in the 1550s. He was the illegitimate son of João de Noronha and nephew of viceroy Afonso de Noronha (1550–1554). input: The official residence of Brazil's president is the Palácio da Alvorada (Portuguese pronunciation: [paˈlasju dawvoˈɾadɐ]). Located in the country's capital city of Brasília, the building sits on a peninsula that juts out into Lake Paranoá. Designed by Oscar Niemeyer, it was built between 1957 and 1958 and follows the principles of modernist architecture. Every Brazilian president since Juscelino Kubitschek has lived there. The building has been designated a National Historic Heritage Site. In addition to serving as a presidential home, the Palácio da Alvorada is also used as a venue for state functions. The president's official workplace and the center of executive power, however, is the Palácio do Planalto.
target: The Palácio da Alvorada (Portuguese pronunciation: [paˈlasju dawvoˈɾadɐ]) is the official residence of the president of Brazil. It is located in the national capital of Brasília, on a peninsula at the margins of Paranoá Lake. The building was designed by Oscar Niemeyer and built between 1957 and 1958 in the modernist style. It has been the residence of every Brazilian president since Juscelino Kubitschek. The building is listed as a National Historic Heritage Site. The Palácio da Alvorada is used as a residence and for official receptions. The president's workplace and center of the executive branch is the Palácio do Planalto.

input: Mountain Swainson-pea, known alternatively as small purple pea, is the common name for *Swainsona recta*, a flowering plant in the Fabaceae family native solely to south-eastern mainland Australia. This perennial grows in an upright or ascending manner and bears imparipinnate leaves made up of 5 to 13 very narrow, linear leaflets. It produces racemes of roughly 6 to more than 25 purple flowers.

input: A tunneling protocol is a network communication method that facilitates the transfer of data between separate networks. For instance, these protocols enable secure private data to traverse public networks like the Internet, or allow one incompatible network protocol to operate across another through a technique known as encapsulation. Since tunneling involves repackaging traffic into an alternate format—often with built-in encryption—it can obscure what type of traffic flows through the tunnel. Tunneling protocols function by utilizing a packet's payload section to transport the packets responsible for delivering the actual service. Although tunneling relies on layered protocol structures similar to OSI and TCP/IP models, it typically circumvents standard layering practices by using the payload to deliver services not ordinarily supported by that network layer. In most cases, the transport protocol operates at the same level or a higher level within the layered framework compared to the service protocol being carried.
target: In computer networks, a tunneling protocol is a communication protocol that allows for the movement of data from one network to another. They can, for example, allow private communications to be sent across a public network (such as the Internet), or for one network protocol to be carried over an incompatible network, through a process called encapsulation. Because tunneling involves repackaging the traffic data into a different form, perhaps with encryption as standard, it can hide the nature of the traffic that is run through a tunnel. Tunneling protocols work by using the data portion of a packet (the payload) to carry the packets that actually provide the service. Tunneling uses a layered protocol model such as those of the OSI or TCP/IP protocol suite, but usually violates the layering when using the payload to carry a service not normally provided by the network. Typically, the delivery protocol operates at an equal or higher level in the layered model than the payload protocol.

input: Smooth Noodle Maps (stylized as smoothnoodlemaps), the eighth studio album by American new wave band Devo, came out in June 1990. It was the band's final release under Enigma Records and was recorded during a three-month span at Master Control Studios in Burbank, California, from October 1989 to January 1990. The album would stand as Devo's last full-length studio work until Something for Everybody was released in 2010, and it was also the final studio album to include drummer David Kendrick. The single "Post Post-Modern Man" rose to No. 7 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart for the week of August 11, 1990, and subsequently hit No. 26 on Billboard's Hot Dance/Club Play chart for the week of September 29, 1990.

Liam Devally (1933–9 April 2018) was born in Cahir, County Tipperary, Ireland, and died in Dublin. An Irish radio and television presenter and singer who later became a barrister and judge, Devally was the son of a Garda. His family relocated to Mullingar, County Westmeath during his childhood. He obtained a scholarship to study at St Enda's College, Galway.

Throughout his broadcasting career, Devally hosted numerous programmes in Ireland. He worked as a radio presenter on RTÉ Radio 1 and gained prominence among Irish audiences between 1972 and 1979, when he provided Eurovision Song Contest commentary for RTÉ Radio. His recordings included My Lagan Love and Eileen Aroon. In 1959, he performed on the Ed Sullivan Show in America, and in 1966, he portrayed Irish revolutionary Eamon Ceant in the dramatisation Insurrection.

input: Lokomby is a settlement and commune located in Madagascar. It is situated within the Manakara district, which itself is located in the Fitovinany region. According to the 2001 commune census, Lokomby had an estimated population of around 15,000 residents. Educational facilities in the town include primary schools and lower secondary schools. Farming is the dominant occupation, with approximately 95% of the commune's residents engaged in agriculture. The principal agricultural outputs are coffee and rice, supplemented by significant production of cloves, lychee, and cassava. The remaining 5% of the population is employed in the service sector.
target: Lokomby is a town and commune in Madagascar. It belongs to the district of Manakara, which is a part of Fitovinany. The majority 95% of the population of the commune are farmers. The most important crops are coffee and rice, while other important agricultural products are cloves, lychee and cassava. input: The Polish surname Mądry (pronounced [ˈmɔndrɨ]) translates to "wise" and can optionally take the feminine form Mądra. Variants include Mondry and Mundry, which represent dialectal or alternative spellings. Related surnames exist in neighboring languages: Czech (Moudrý), Slovak (Múdry), and Ukrainian (Mudry). Among those bearing this surname are Ilona Mądra, a Polish basketball player born in 1966, and Maria Ilnicka-Mądry, a Polish politician who lived from 1946 to 2023.
target: Mądry (Polish pronunciation: [ˈmɔndrɨ]; optional feminine: Mądra) is a Polish surname meaning "wise". input: The Eurovision Debate is a live televised event produced by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU), in which the top political candidates vying for the role of European Commission President — referred to as "Spitzenkandidaten" — face off on screen. Organized by the European Parliament and held in Brussels, Belgium, the debate is distributed across Europe via the Eurovision network. Ludwig Hirzel, a Swiss literary historian, was born in Zürich on 23 February 1838 and died on 1 June 1897. His father, Ludwig Hirzel (1801–1841), was a professor of theology at the University of Zürich. Hirzel earned his doctorate from the University of Zürich in 1862 and subsequently pursued a career in secondary education, teaching in Frauenfeld (1862) and later at the cantonal school in Aarau (1866). From 1874 until his death in 1897, he served as professor of German language and literature at the University of Berne.

Among Hirzel's academic contributions were studies of major literary figures including Goethe, Schiller, and Wieland. He is best known for his definitive editions of Albrecht von Haller's poetry (1882) and journals (1883). He also authored an essay on Swiss mathematician Conrad Dasypodius and edited two of Wieland's works: Geschichte der Gelehrtheit (History of the Scholars) and Beziehungen zu den deutschen Romantikern (Connections to the German Romanticists).

input: DELTA, which stands for DEscription Language for TAxonomy, is a data format employed in taxonomic work to document characteristics of organisms. Created with computer processing in mind, it enables the production of identification keys, diagnostic information, and similar outputs. It has become a widely recognized standard, with numerous applications available for different taxonomic applications. The format was developed by CSIRO's Australian Division of Entomology between 1971 and 2000, with Dr. Michael J. Dallwitz playing a significant role in its creation. In more recent years, the Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) converted the DELTA software to Java, making it compatible with Java environments and compatible across different operating systems. The software is now available for download through the ALA website.
target: DELTA (DEscription Language for TAxonomy) is a data format used in taxonomy for recording descriptions of living things. It is designed for computer processing, allowing the generation of identification keys, diagnosis, etc. It is widely accepted as a standard and many programs using this format are available for various taxonomic tasks. It was devised by the CSIRO Australian Division of Entomology in 1971 to 2000, with a notable part taken by Dr. Michael J. Dallwitz. More recently, the Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) rewrote the DELTA software in Java so it can run in a Java environment and across multiple operating systems. The software package can now be found at and downloaded from the ALA site.

input: The Rush County Courthouse, constructed in 1888, is located at 715 Elm St. in La Crosse, Kansas. This two-story building features brick construction in a common bond pattern and includes a full basement. The building was financed through a $20,000 bond measure that voters approved on July 10, 1888.

Kothagudem Assembly constituency is a legislative assembly constituency in Telangana, India. Located within Bhadradri Kothagudem district, it encompasses the municipalities of Kothagudem and Palwancha, as well as a portion of the Khammam Lok Sabha constituency. 

Jalagam Venkat Rao currently serves as the representative for this constituency in his second term. input: Solute pumping is the mechanism by which active transport moves solutes across cell membranes, allowing molecules to pass through the lipid bilayer even when obstacles such as concentration gradients or molecular polarity would otherwise block their movement. This process relies on protein channels that enable molecules to enter cells. Unlike diffusion, which is a passive process requiring no cellular energy, solute pumping is active in nature, consuming ATP to change the shape of protein channels and thus allowing molecules that could not otherwise cross the membrane passively to pass through.
target: Solute pumping is a form of active transport of a solute through a cell membrane. Solute pumping allows a molecule that cannot regularly cross the lipid bilayer (because of concentration gradient, polarity, or other reasons) to enter the cell by way of a protein channel. Unlike diffusion (a form of passive transport), solute pumping requires energy (provided by ATP) to change the shape of the protein channel to allow the molecule to pass through, which is why it is an active transport mechanism.

input: A 1982 Canadian thriller directed by Max Fischer and starring Irene Cara, George Segal, Clark Johnson, and Nicholas Campbell, *Killing 'em Softly* is best known today for the major production troubles it encountered. Irene Cara also provides the vocals for the film's opening theme song, "City Nights".

input: *Sminthopsis butleri*, known commonly as Butler's dunnart or the Carpentarian dunnart, is a small marsupial that is a close relative of the Kakadu dunnart. Like that species, it has a soft, fluffy coat whose upper surface ranges in colour from brown to mouse grey, while its underside is white. The body measures 75-88mm from head to anus, and the tail adds another 72-90mm, for a total length of 147-178mm. Adults typically weigh 10-20g, a range that reflects variations in sex, habitat, and food availability.

input: Kalle Petter Huttunen, known as Pekka (born 2 August 1871 in Rantasalmi, died 24 November 1932 in Petrozavodsk), was a Finnish politician and tenant farmer. From 1907 to 1918, he served as a member of the Finnish Parliament as a representative of the Social Democratic Party of Finland (SDP). When the Finnish Civil War broke out, Huttunen aligned himself with the Red faction. Following the defeat and dissolution of the Finnish Socialist Workers' Republic, he relocated to the Soviet Union. He eventually made his home in the Karelian ASSR.
target: Kalle Petter (Pekka) Huttunen (2 August 1871, Rantasalmi — 24 November 1932, Petrozavodsk) was a Finnish tenant farmer and politician. During the Finnish Civil War Huttunen sided with the Reds, and after the collapse of the Finnish Socialist Workers' Republic he fled to Soviet Russia. He later settled in the Karelian ASSR.

input: The Chapel of Saint Catherine, also referred to as the Church of Saint Catherine (known in Latin as *Ecclesia Sanctae Catharinae*; in Arabic as كنيسة القديسة كترينا; and in Hebrew as כנסיית קתרינה הקדושה), is a Roman Catholic house of worship located adjacent to the northern wall of the Basilica of the Nativity in Bethlehem, within the Palestinian territory of the West Bank. The building serves a dual purpose, functioning as both a parish church and a Franciscan monastery. A network of underground caves lies beneath the structure. The institution is administered by the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem, follows the Roman Rite tradition, and has held UNESCO World Heritage Site status since 2012 as part of the "Birthplace of Jesus" World Heritage designation.
target: The Church of Saint Catherine or Chapel of Saint Catherine (Latin: Ecclesia Sanctae Catharinae, Arabic: كنيسة القديسة كترينا, Hebrew: כנסיית קתרינה הקדושה) is a Catholic religious building located adjacent to the northern part of the Basilica of the Nativity in Bethlehem in the West Bank, Palestine. It works as a parish church and Franciscan monastery. There is a complex of caves underneath the church. It is administered by the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem, follows the Roman Rite, and is included in the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2012 as part of the "Birthplace of Jesus" World Heritage Site.

input: The Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (UERJ) is a major public research institution situated in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil. UERJ operates additional campuses throughout the region, including facilities in Petrópolis, Nova Friburgo (which houses the Polytechnic Institute), Teresópolis, Duque de Caxias, Angra dos Reis, Resende, and São Gonçalo.

input: Bassline, which goes by several other names including bassline house, 4x4, and niche, is a style of electronic dance music that originated in South Yorkshire in the early 2000s. The genre is defined by a distinctive four-on-the-floor beat running at roughly 135–142 beats per minute, prominent bass sounds that draw comparisons to speed garage, chopped-up vocal samples taken from R&B and pop songs, and an overall pop-friendly aesthetic. During the genre's early years, Niche Nightclub in Sheffield was the most significant venue in the bassline scene, a status it held until it was embroiled in public controversy after a police operation resulted in its permanent closure in 2005.
target: Bassline (sometimes referred to as bassline house or 4x4 or niche) is a genre of electronic dance music that originated in South Yorkshire in the early 2000s. Stylistically it comprises a four-to-the-floor beat with a tempo of around 135–142 beats per minute and a heavy bass, similar to speed garage, with chopped up R&B and Pop vocal samples and a pop music aesthetic. Particularly in the scene's early days, the most prominent bassline club was Sheffield's Niche Nightclub, which became the centre of controversy due to a police raid which resulted in the club's closure in 2005.

input: The Gyrokinetic ElectroMagnetic (GEM) code is a simulation tool designed for gyrokinetic plasma turbulence that employs the δf {\displaystyle \delta f} particle-in-cell method. Its primary aim is investigating waves, instabilities, and nonlinear dynamics in tokamak fusion plasmas. Additional details regarding GEM are available on its dedicated web page. GEM is available in two forms: a flux-tube version and a global general geometry version. Both versions rely on a field-aligned coordinate system. The code handles ions kinetically through gyro-orbit averaging, whereas electrons are handled using a drift-kinetic method.

input: The Pasquino Group—also called Menelaus Carrying the Body of Patroclus or Ajax Carrying the Body of Achilles—comprises marble sculptures modeled on an original Hellenistic bronze created around 200–150 BCE. Scholars have identified at least fifteen Roman marble copies of this work. These copies possess intricate artistic and cultural histories that reveal the extent of the improvised "restorations" performed on damaged fragments of ancient Roman sculptures during the 16th and 17th centuries, a period when Italian sculptors added new and frequently arbitrary, damaging elements to reconstruct the missing portions of ancient works. One of the most renowned versions of this composition—though so severely fragmented and worn that its subject is hardly recognizable at first sight—is the famous Pasquin, one of Rome's celebrated talking statues. It was set upon a pedestal in 1501 and has never undergone restoration. A variant of the group, apparently intended to depict other figures from Homer's epics, appears among the Sperlonga sculptures, which were discovered in 1957.

Many of these marble copies have complex artistic and social histories that illustrate the degree to which improvisatory "restorations" were made to fragments of ancient Roman sculpture during the 16th and 17th centuries, in which contemporary Italian sculptors made original and often arbitrary and destructive additions in an effort to replace lost fragments of the ancient sculptures. One of the most famous versions of the composition, though so dismembered and battered that the relationship is scarcely recognizable at first glance, is the so-called Pasquin, one of the talking statues of Rome. It was set up on a pedestal in 1501 and remains unrestored. A version of the group, probably intended to represent other Homeric figures, is part of the Sperlonga sculptures found in 1957.

input: The Martyrs of Nicomedia represent an important group of Christians who, according to tradition, perished in the Roman city of Nicomedia during the Roman Empire's persecution of Christians. Christian historical accounts maintain that numerous believers were executed in this city during the early 300s because they would not abandon their faith or make sacrifices to the Roman gods. These occurrences are typically linked to the concluding stage of the Diocletianic Persecution, which scholars call the Great Persecution—the fiercest assault on Christians by the Roman Empire before Constantine the Great made Christianity legal. Later Byzantine writings document what is portrayed as an especially savage massacre on Christmas Day in 304 AD, when a large assembly of Christians observing the birth of Jesus was reportedly slaughtered for declining to participate in pagan sacrificial ceremonies. Christian historical texts provide conflicting figures regarding how many died. Certain sources cite thousands of casualties, whereas later religious works document 20,000 martyrs at Nicomedia. Contemporary historians commonly view the larger figures as legendary or religiously exaggerated rather than historically reliable.
target: The Martyrs of Nicomedia refer to a large group of Christians traditionally believed to have been killed in the Roman city of Nicomedia during the persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire. According to Christian tradition, thousands of Christians were killed in the city during the early fourth century after refusing to renounce their faith or offer sacrifices to the Roman gods. The events are usually connected with the final phase of the Diocletianic Persecution, often referred to by historians as the Great Persecution, the most extensive persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire prior to the legalization of Christianity under Constantine the Great. Later Byzantine traditions describe a particularly large massacre occurring on Christmas Day in 304 AD, when a large gathering of Christians celebrating the Nativity of Jesus was reportedly killed after refusing to participate in pagan sacrificial rites. The number of victims recorded in Christian sources varies widely. Some accounts describe several thousand victims, while later liturgical texts refer to 20,000 martyrs who died in Nicomedia. Modern historians generally treat the larger number as symbolic or hagiographical rather than a precise historical count.

input: Adır Island (Turkish: Adır Adası), also called Lim Island (Armenian: Լիմ կղզի, romanized: Lim kghzi), is the largest island in Lake Van, situated in the lake's northeastern part. During the Armenian genocide, more than 12,000 Armenian women and children escaped to the island over a span of three days, while a small group of men—approximately several dozen—held off Hamidiye regiments to safeguard their flight. Conditions rapidly worsened owing to a severe shortage of food. The island contains Lim Monastery, an Armenian monastery developed over many centuries. According to Armenian historical records, the monastery existed prior to 884, though tradition maintains that St. Gregory the Illuminator established it in the 4th century. By the 14th century, the complex included three churches: Surp Astvatsatsin, Surp Garabed, and Surp Kevork. A bell tower, chapel, and parish residence were built in 1766. The monastery stayed in use until 1918, after which it entered a steady decline. An ornately decorated altar curtain from the monastery has been preserved in remarkable condition and is now exhibited at the San Lazzaro Island museum in Venice.
target: Adır Island (Turkish: Adır Adası) or Lim Island (Armenian: Լիմ կղզի, romanized: Lim kghzi), is the largest island in Lake Van, located in the northeastern side of the lake. During the Armenian genocide upwards of 12,000 Armenian women and children, crossed to the isle over a period of three days while a few dozen men covered their retreat from Hamidiye regiments. The situation soon became critical because of a lack of food. Lim Monastery was built by Armenians over the centuries on the island, with Armenian sources indicating the monastery was already founded pre-884, with tradition saying that St. Gregory the Illuminator himself founded it in the 4th century. By the 14th century there were Surp Astvatsatsin, Surp Garabed and Surp Kevork churches. In 1766 the belltower, a chapel and a parish house were built. The monastery functioned until 1918, and has deteriorated ever since. The large, intricate curtain from one of the altars is preserved in very good condition at the museum of San Lazzaro Island in Venice.

input: D. Antão de Noronha was appointed viceroy of India by Portugal's King Sebastian in 1564. Prior to this role, he had served at Ceuta during the 1540s and held a captaincy at Hormuz in the 1550s. An illegitimate son of João de Noronha, he was also a nephew of Afonso de Noronha, who had previously served as viceroy from 1550 to 1554. Antão de Noronha's rule over Portuguese India lasted from 3 September 1564 to September 1568. Among his notable achievements during this period was the conquest of Mangalore and the construction of a fort there in 1568. He died in 1569 while making the sea voyage back to Portugal.

input: The Palácio da Alvorada (Portuguese pronunciation: [paˈlasju dawvoˈɾadɐ]) is the official home of Brazil's president. Situated in Brasília, the nation's capital, the structure rests on a peninsula extending into Lake Paranoá. The work of architect Oscar Niemeyer, it was constructed from 1957 to 1958 in accordance with modernist architectural principles. It has been the residence of every Brazilian president beginning with Juscelino Kubitschek. The building holds the status of a National Historic Heritage Site. Beyond functioning as the presidential residence, the Palácio da Alvorada also hosts state events. Nevertheless, the president's official office and the seat of executive authority is the Palácio do Planalto.

UWA-001, also referred to as α-phenyl-MDMA and methylenedioxymephenidine, is a phenethylamine-based compound developed at the University of Western Australia. It was created as a safer alternative to 3,4-methylenedioxy-N-methylamphetamine (MDMA) and has been studied for its possible use in treating Parkinson's disease. 

In terms of receptor binding, UWA-001 demonstrates a 5-HT2A receptor affinity of 1.2 μM (approximately 10 times higher than MDMA), a serotonin transporter affinity of 1.3 μM (roughly 4 times lower than MDMA), a norepinephrine transporter affinity of 13.4 μM (about 26 times higher than MDMA), and minimal dopamine transporter affinity (greater than 50 μM). 

Distinctively from MDMA and para-methoxyamphetamine, though similarly to ketamine, UWA-001 enhances prepulse inhibition. This characteristic led researchers to conclude it lacked psychoactive properties, though testing at other binding sites was not conducted. While the compound exhibits toxicity toward the SH-SY5Y cell line at elevated concentrations, it remains substantially less toxic than MDMA across all tested concentration levels.

Structurally, UWA-001 shares similarities with diarylethylamines including lefetamine (a stimulant and opioid agent) and ephenidine (a dissociative anesthetic that functions as an NMDA receptor antagonist).
target: UWA-001 (also known as α-phenyl-MDMA and methylenedioxymephenidine) is a phenethylamine derivative invented at the University of Western Australia as non-toxic alternative to 3,4-methylenedioxy-N-methylamphetamine (MDMA) and researched as a potential treatment for Parkinson's disease. It has a 5-HT2A receptor affinity of 1.2 μM (~10-fold increase compared to MDMA), 1.3 μM for the serotonin transporter (~4-fold decrease compared to MDMA), 13.4 μM for the norepinephrine transporter (~26-fold increase compared to MDMA) and virtually no affinity for the dopamine transporter (>50 μM). Unlike MDMA and para-methoxyamphetamine (but similarly to ketamine), UWA-001 increases prepulse inhibition and was therefore considered to be non-psychoactive, though it was not assayed at other binding sites. It is toxic to the SH-SY5Y cell line at high concentrations, however significantly less toxic than MDMA at all concentrations tested. UWA-001 is structurally related to the diarylethylamines lefetamine (a stimulant and opioid) and the dissociative anesthetic ephenidine, which acts as a NMDA receptor antagonist.

input: Lee Cronin and his team developed assembly theory as a method for measuring molecular and object complexity by calculating the fewest steps needed to construct them from basic building blocks. The theory introduces an assembly index—a quantifiable metric that reflects how structurally intricate a molecule is. Cronin's group contends that this method enables empirical testing and can be applied to studying selection mechanisms, evolutionary processes, and recognizing biosignatures in the field of astrobiology. Nevertheless, experts have questioned the practical value of this method.
target: Assembly theory is a framework developed to quantify the complexity of molecules and objects by assessing the minimal number of steps required to assemble them from fundamental building blocks. Proposed by chemist Lee Cronin and his team, the theory assigns an assembly index to molecules, which serves as a measurable indicator of their structural complexity. Cronin and colleagues argue that this approach allows for experimental verification and has applications in understanding selection processes, evolution, and the identification of biosignatures in astrobiology. However, the usefulness of the approach has been disputed.

input: Songs of the Southern Skies is a studio album that was collaboratively produced by Australian singer-songwriter Katie Noonan and Australian classical guitarist Karin Schaupp. Released in August 2012, the album reached number 97 on the ARIA physical albums chart and number 3 on the classical chart. It features classical, folk, jazz, and pop music from Australia and New Zealand. Recorded in Brisbane, the album features guest appearances by Iva Davies, Gurrumul, Whirimako Black, Diana Doherty, Clare Bowditch, and Chris Cheney. Noonan described the project this way: "this project brings together my two main musical loves – classical and pop music. As an artist I love blurring the boundaries of genre and hearing musical worlds collide. This project is a wonderful opportunity for Karin and I to do exactly that!" A tour supporting the album was held throughout 2013. At the 2012 ARIA Music Awards, Songs of the Southern Skies received nominations for both 'Best Adult Contemporary' album, which was ultimately won by The Ol' Razzle Dazzle by Missy Higgins, and 'Best Independent Release', which was ultimately won by Prisoner by The Jezabels.

input: A tunneling protocol is a method of network communication that enables data to be transferred across different networks. For example, such protocols allow confidential private data to travel over public networks such as the Internet, or permit an incompatible network protocol to function over another through a process called encapsulation. Because tunneling involves wrapping traffic in a different format—frequently with encryption included—it can hide the nature of the traffic passing through the tunnel. Tunneling protocols work by using a packet's payload section to carry the packets responsible for delivering the intended service. Although tunneling depends on layered protocol architectures similar to the OSI and TCP/IP models, it generally bypasses conventional layering conventions by using the payload to provide services not typically supported at that network layer. In most instances, the transport protocol operates at the same layer or a higher layer within the layered architecture relative to the service protocol it is carrying.
target: In computer networks, a tunneling protocol is a communication protocol that allows for the movement of data from one network to another. They can, for example, allow private communications to be sent across a public network (such as the Internet), or for one network protocol to be carried over an incompatible network, through a process called encapsulation. Because tunneling involves repackaging the traffic data into a different form, perhaps with encryption as standard, it can hide the nature of the traffic that is run through a tunnel. Tunneling protocols work by using the data portion of a packet (the payload) to carry the packets that actually provide the service. Tunneling uses a layered protocol model such as those of the OSI or TCP/IP protocol suite, but usually violates the layering when using the payload to carry a service not normally provided by the network. Typically, the delivery protocol operates at an equal or higher level in the layered model than the payload protocol.

Born in Cahir, County Tipperary, Ireland, Liam Devally (1933–9 April 2018) passed away in Dublin. An Irish presenter of radio and television and a singer who went on to become a barrister and judge, Devally was the son of a Garda officer. During his childhood, his family moved to Mullingar, County Westmeath. He was awarded a scholarship to attend St Enda's College in Galway.

Over the course of his broadcasting career, Devally presented many programmes throughout Ireland. He served as a radio presenter on RTÉ Radio 1 and became well known to Irish audiences between 1972 and 1979, during which time he provided commentary on the Eurovision Song Contest for RTÉ Radio. Among his recordings were My Lagan Love and Eileen Aroon. In 1959, he appeared on the Ed Sullivan Show in America, and in 1966, he played the role of Irish revolutionary Eamon Ceant in the dramatisation Insurrection.

Devally wed Mairead Connaghton, a woman he met while working at RTÉ, and the couple made their home in Blackrock, County Dublin. He went on to pursue a career in law as a barrister and served as a Circuit Court judge from 1991 until he retired. He died in Dublin at the age of 85 and was buried in Kilmacanogue Cemetery, County Wicklow.

input: Lokomby is a commune and settlement found in Madagascar, specifically within the Manakara district, which falls under the Fitovinany region. The 2001 commune census estimated the population at approximately 15,000 people. The town is served by both primary and lower secondary schools. Agriculture is the predominant livelihood, employing roughly 95% of the commune's population. Coffee and rice are the main crops produced, with cloves, lychee, and cassava also representing notable outputs. The remaining 5% of residents work in the service sector.

input: Sylwester Janiszewski, born on 24 January 1988, is a retired Polish professional racing cyclist. Ludwig Hirzel was a Swiss literary historian, born in Zürich on 23 February 1838 and died on 1 June 1897. His father, Ludwig Hirzel (1801–1841), held a professorship in theology at the University of Zürich. Hirzel received his doctorate from the University of Zürich in 1862 and went on to a career in secondary education, teaching in Frauenfeld (1862) and later at the cantonal school in Aarau (1866). From 1874 until his death in 1897, he held the position of professor of German language and literature at the University of Berne.

Hirzel's scholarly work included studies of prominent literary figures such as Goethe, Schiller, and Wieland. He is most renowned for his authoritative editions of Albrecht von Haller's poetry (1882) and journals (1883). In addition, he wrote an essay on the Swiss mathematician Conrad Dasypodius and edited two of Wieland's works: Geschichte der Gelehrtheit (History of the Scholars) and Beziehungen zu den deutschen Romantikern (Connections to the German Romanticists).

input: The British rock band the Pretenders released "Where Has Everybody Gone?" in 1987. The band contributed two tracks to The Living Daylights, a 1987 James Bond film soundtrack: "Where Has Everybody Gone?" and "If There Was a Man". The Living Daylights soundtrack features both songs along with an instrumental remix of "Where Has Everybody Gone?". input: DELTA, an acronym for DEscription Language for TAxonomy, is a data format used in taxonomic research to record the characteristics of organisms. Designed with automated processing in mind, it supports the generation of identification keys, diagnostic descriptions, and related outputs. The format has gained widespread recognition as a standard, with many software applications developed to support various taxonomic purposes. It was created by the Australian Division of Entomology at CSIRO between 1971 and 2000, with Dr. Michael J. Dallwitz serving as a key contributor to its development. More recently, the Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) ported the DELTA software to Java, enabling it to function within Java environments and across multiple operating systems. The software can now be downloaded from the ALA website.

input: The Langenberg (pronounced [ˈlaŋənbɛʁk] in German) is a stretched chalk mountain positioned between Göttingerode to the south and Harlingerode to the north. It is located in Bad Harzburg, a resort town situated in the Goslar district within Lower Saxony, Germany. The site has achieved significant geological importance at the national level for two main reasons: the prominent visibility of the Northern Harz Boundary Fault that can be observed in the Langenberg chalk quarry, and the 1998 discovery of Europasaurus fossils within that same quarry.
target: The Langenberg (German pronunciation: [ˈlaŋənbɛʁk] ) is an elongated chalk hill north of Göttingerode and south of Harlingerode in the spa town of Bad Harzburg in Goslar district, in the German state of Lower Saxony. Due to its obvious display of the Northern Harz Boundary Fault in the Langenberg chalk quarry and the discovery of the Europasaurus in 1998 in said quarry, this mountain has gained national geological relevance.

input: Solute pumping is the process through which active transport carries solutes across cell membranes, enabling molecules to move through the lipid bilayer even when barriers like concentration gradients or molecular polarity would otherwise prevent their passage. This mechanism depends on protein channels that allow molecules to enter cells. In contrast to diffusion, a passive process that demands no cellular energy, solute pumping is active, using ATP to alter the shape of protein channels and thereby permitting molecules that could not otherwise cross the membrane passively to move through.
target: Solute pumping is a form of active transport of a solute through a cell membrane. Solute pumping allows a molecule that cannot regularly cross the lipid bilayer (because of concentration gradient, polarity, or other reasons) to enter the cell by way of a protein channel. Unlike diffusion (a form of passive transport), solute pumping requires energy (provided by ATP) to change the shape of the protein channel to allow the molecule to pass through, which is why it is an active transport mechanism.

input: American film and theatre actress Jane Fenmore Barnes lived from August 17, 1910, to March 20, 1998, and was prominent during the 1930s. Originally pursuing a career as a concert pianist, she eventually chose acting instead. She spent considerable time performing in theatrical productions, radio dramas, and modeling work before joining Fox Studios as a film actress. Between 1934 and 1937, she appeared in numerous significant and supporting film roles. Afterward, she devoted herself to theatre to develop her craft, and in August 1937, she married actor Carlyle Moore Jr. When her Broadway theatre aspirations in New York proved unsuccessful, she transitioned to work as a newspaper columnist and relocated multiple times between Massachusetts and Hollywood. Later in life, she moved to Victorville, California, where she remained and participated in her local library organization, reflecting her passion for reading.
target: Jane Fenmore Barnes (August 17, 1910 – March 20, 1998) was an American film and theatre actress during the 1930s. Cast in multiple major and minor film roles from 1934 through 1937, she then returned to theatre work to hone her acting skills before marrying actor Carlyle Moore Jr. in August 1937. When her theatre plans in New York on Broadway did not work out, she became a columnist for multiple papers, moving several times back to Massachusetts and then Hollywood. input: Vladimir Ivanovich Staël von Holstein, Baron (Russian: Владимир Иванович Сталь фон Гольштейн; 29 June 1853 – 21 September 1921), was a lieutenant general in the Russian imperial army. Throughout his military service, he was primarily stationed at the Petersburg Military District's staff. Beginning in 1908, he held the position of vice-commandant at the Peter and Paul Fortress, which he commanded when the February Revolution took place.
